WHAT IT IS
It is build 3's runner (archived at out/build3/run_m3.py) with one label changed. The change follows gate addendum A10, the gate's correction to checklist item 10 of the execution note.

THE ONE CHANGE TO WHAT THE RUN WRITES
- The engine label on every throughput record now reads exactly: "LAMMPS 29Aug2024, compiled from source on the box, GPU package, CUDA sm_80".
- It replaces "LAMMPS 2024.08.29, conda-forge CUDA build, GPU package". That wording was false once the engine moved to a source compile.
- This is one constant (LABEL_ENGINE, line 138). Its comment now cites the addendum.
- The other two labels are unchanged: "one box, 11,250 atoms" and "GPU package mixed precision".
- The true engine facts beside the label are unchanged. These are the version line, the cmake command, the source address and checksum, and the fast Fourier transform library choice.

WHAT THE SELFTEST NOW TIES TO THE LABEL (two new checks)
- Build 3's checks compared the records with the constant itself. A wrong constant would have passed them.
- New check 1: the throughput record's labels must equal the note's text, copied by hand into the selftest. This follows build 3's own pattern for the cmake flags.
- New check 2: the old "conda-forge" wording must appear in no output file of any planted scenario.

NOTHING ELSE CHANGED
- The deck edits, dry run, equilibration fallback and production runs are unchanged.
- The endpoint arithmetic, validity propagation and guards are unchanged too.
- The diff against build 3 is the constant, its comment, and the two checks.
- The design has no dispersion rule, so there is no zero-dispersion case to plant.

It is rewritten byte for byte from build 3 (out/build3/onbox_m3.sh). It never carried the engine label, so the label change does not touch it. It never ran here. The bash syntax check passes. The selftest checks its text (23 checks).

WHAT IT DOES, IN THE NOTE'S ORDER
1. The cost and time guard runs first. The compile gets at most 1,800 s.
2. It records the GPU report (nvidia-smi) and checks that the CUDA compiler, g++ and make exist.
3. It uses the image's cmake if found. Otherwise it runs "python3 -m pip install --user cmake", the one allowed install.
4. It downloads the stable_29Aug2024 source from GitHub, or from the LAMMPS mirror on failure. It records the address, checksum and size.
5. It unpacks into ~/m3_run/engine_src/. It picks FFTW3 if /usr/include/fftw3.h exists, else KISS.
6. It runs the note's cmake command exactly, then builds on every processor and installs into ~/m3_run/engine/.
7. Then the stages run in order: engine check, dry run, box copy, equilibration, the three production runs, endpoints.
- Results go to ~/m3_run/results_m3/out/. A RUN_DONE marker carries the exit code.

ON THE TASK TEMPLATE'S VIRTUAL ENVIRONMENT
- The task template asks for a Python virtual environment and installs. The execution note binds over it.
- The note allows one install only (cmake, if missing) and no conda. The runner needs only Python's standard library.
- So there is no virtual environment, as in build 3.

FAILURE HANDLING
- A failed compile step gives code 2 and a void run. Hitting the time cap is recorded as exit 124.
- Any nonzero stage code voids the run, writes the summary, and writes RUN_DONE with that code.

built.expected:
Unchanged from build 3: the label change alters no stage, timing or file count.

WALL-CLOCK (at most 7,200 s on the box: USD 3.98 at USD 1.99 per hour, under the USD 5 launch budget)
- First, the bootstrap installs its unused Python packages. That time is unmeasured.
- Download and compile: unmeasured, capped at 1,800 s (USD 0.995). The guard plans for the full 1,800 s.
- At the card's 250 ns/day, the engine does 1,446.76 steps per second.
  - The equilibration's 500,000 steps take about 346 s, plus up to 10,000 energy-minimisation evaluations.
  - Each production run's 125,000 steps take about 86 s. The dry run's 2,000 steps take about 1.4 s.
- At 100 ns/day, those become about 864 s and 216 s.
- Each run also has engine start-up time. Run a, with its per-step sampling, should be the slowest of the three.
- The per-atom step rate at 250 ns/day would be 1.6276e7 atom-steps per second.

FILES IN results_m3/out/ AFTER A FULL RUN
- 30 record files:
  - 10 endpoint records, with the throughput claim, the gate and the re-pricing kept apart.
  - 14 check records: the timed dry run, ten instrument checks, the engine package check, the deck edits and the equilibration fallback.
  - 6 run records: dry run, box copy, equilibration, runs a, b and c.
- Raw rows:
  - raw_runs.jsonl: 5 rows, or 6 if the equilibration needs its second attempt.
  - raw_thermo.jsonl: about 191 rows. That is 4 from the dry run, about 106 from the equilibration and 27 per production run.
  - guard_rows.jsonl: 9 rows, or 10 with a second equilibration attempt.
- Run files: RUN_VALID.json, stages.json, labels.json, env.txt, m3_summary.json, RUN_DONE and onbox_m3.log.
- labels.json and every throughput record carry the new label "LAMMPS 29Aug2024, compiled from source on the box, GPU package, CUDA sm_80".
- Compile files: compile_record.txt, download.log, the three cmake logs and toolchain_versions.txt. Also lmp_help.txt, lmp_ldd.txt and two nvidia-smi files.
- cmake_pip.log appears only if the image has no cmake.
- Simulation files: every LAMMPS log and screen capture, the density file and the dry-run date stamps. Also the edited decks with their diffs.
- Only the first and last 5 lines of each sample file come back. The note expects 20,000 rows each for run a. The count is recorded, not judged.

IF THE COMPILE FAILS
- Code 2 and a void run. No endpoint record is written. The summary restates the failure and the last 40 lines of the failing step's log.
- If the engine lacks a required package: code 2, one check record saying NOT_LISTED with the missing name, and no simulation run.

NOT VERIFIED ON ANY BOX (carried from build 3)
- The LAMMPS GPU build needs CUDA's bin2c tool and cmake's older CUDA finder. This image may lack either. A failure stops at configure with code 2.
- The GPU package may compile for several GPU generations by default. The build may run long. The 1,800 s cap bounds it.
- The deck's per-atom stress and heat-flux computes may not run with the GPU pair style. A refusal naming them is handled. Any other error stops the run.
- The dry run starts from the raw packed box at a 2 fs step. If that is unstable, the run stops with code 10.
